facts.statement: The genus Lamarqueavis was named in 2010 by Agnolin, with the type species L. australis based on a partial right coracoid fossil found in the Allen Formation of Argentina.
facts.quote: The type species, L. australis, was named in 2010 and is based on the holotype MML 207, a partial right coracoid found in the Allen Formation, Argentina.

facts.statement: Lamarqueavis lived during the Late Cretaceous period and its fossils have been found in Argentina, Canada, and the United States.
facts.quote: Lamarqueavis is an extinct genus of ornithuran dinosaurs from the family Cimolopterygidae known from Late Cretaceous-aged rocks from Argentina, Canada, and the United States.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MML 207 is an incomplete right coracoid that preserves the proximal articular surfaces and is housed in the Municipal Museum of Lamarque.
facts.quote: El holotipo de esta especie es MML 207 y forma parte de la colección en el Museo Municipal de Lamarque. Se trata de un coracoides derecho incompleto pero que conserva las carillas articulares proximales.

facts.statement: Despite being fragmentary, the presence of a triradiate concavity in the coracoid distinguishes Lamarqueavis from Enantiornithes and links it to basal Neornithes.
facts.quote: Si bien el material es fragmentario ciertas características de este material permiten diferenciarlo de Enantiornithes (principalmente la presencia de una concavidad triósea) y relacionarlo con las especies de Neornithes basales.

facts.statement: The discovery of Lamarqueavis in the Allen Formation, which shows signs of tidal action, supports the hypothesis that early Neornithes lived in coastal environments while Enantiornithes inhabited continental areas.
facts.quote: El hallazgo de Lamarqueavis en la Formación Allen, en la cual se encontraron signos de la acción de mareas, y de otros materiales relacionados a orniturinos derivados parece apoyar la hipótesis que las primeras Neornithes vivieron en ambientes costeros mientras que las Enantiornithes se encontraban en ambientes continentales.

facts.statement: Recent analyses have raised doubts about the validity of the Cimolopterygidae clade and the ability to identify the synapomorphies that support it.
facts.quote: Pero un análisis más reciente de esta y otras especies asignadas a Cimolopterygidae plantea dudas sobre la asignación del clado y la capacidad de reconocer sinapomorfias que lo sustenten.

facts.statement: Lamarqueavis lived from 72.2 to 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The generic name Lamarqueavis is derived from Lamarque, a locality near the fossil site, and avis, the Latin word for 'bird'.
facts.quote: Su nombre genérico se deriva de Lamarque (una localidad cercana al yacimiento) y avis (del latin para ”ave”)

rejected.statement: Lamarqueavis is classified in the family Cimolopterygidae based on specific traits including a ventrally oriented humeral articular facet, a sternally extended procoracoid process forming a thin lamina, and a large ventrally positioned supracoracoid nerve foramen.
rejected.quote: Lamarqueavis autralis and Lamarqueavis sp. were placed in Cimolopterygidae based on the family's traits; a humeral articular facet that's ventrally oriented, a sternally extended procoracoid process that developed into a thin lamina, and a large ventrally positioned supracoracoid nerve foramen.
